paper_metadata.title: Quantifying the advantages of applying quantum approximate algorithms to portfolio optimisation

experiments.description: Baseline QAOA portfolio solver on the DGMVP using binary block encoding, max-biased initial state, hard nearest-neighbour mixer, and classical optimization under shot noise.

algorithm.variant: DGMVP QAOA with max-biased initial state and hard mixing operator
algorithm.ansatz: Alternating cost operator and hard mixer H_tt'(β) / M1(β)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Optimizer stopped by maximum expectation-value evaluations I or optimizer termination; DA uses soft cap I=2000 and COBYLA uses its internal termination criteria
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Random initial ansatz parameters for p=1 in layerwise studies; otherwise random initial parameters for fixed-ansatz runs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary block encoding with l binary variables per asset; weight wt = sum_k 2^(k-1) a z_t^k and a = 1/(2^l - 1)
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_w w^T Σ w subject to w^T 1_n = 1, 0 ≤ w_i ≤ 1, and w_i/a ∈ Z
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard mixer preserves budget constraint; post-selection used in some noisy experiments but not in this baseline noiseless/stochastic-noise optimization setup
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: C = a^2/2 Σ_{i<j} Σ_{k1,k2} σ_ij b_k1 b_k2 Z_i^{k1} Z_j^{k2} + a^2/4 Σ_i Σ_{k1≠k2} σ_ii b_k1 b_k2 Z_i^{k1} Z_i^{k2} - a/2 Σ_i Σ_k \tilde{σ}_i b_k Z_i^k + c

problem_instance.description: Randomly generated DGMVP instances from real market covariance matrices; benchmarked on n=4, l=4 in optimizer studies and n=4, l=5 in mixer-landscape studies

dataset_specification.description: 32 stocks from NASDAQ and NYSE; daily adjusted-close prices from 2023-03-01 to 2023-06-30 over 100 days; example tickers include MSFT, AMZN, ABBV, JPM, PG, AAPL, V, TMO

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Covariance matrix computed from daily adjusted-close prices; random DGMVP instances sampled from market covariance matrices
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 stochastic simulations for many plots; single-instance optimizer scans for Fig. 7; fixed p=10 in landscape scan; exact expectation values estimated with NM=2^22 shots for landscape analysis

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Build covariance matrix; binary block encode weights; prepare max-biased initial state
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Estimate expectation values from sampled bitstrings; compute approximation ratios α_mean and α_min

speedup_claims.factor: power-law scaling with exponent b = 0.76 ± 0.30 (warm-started) and b = 0.51 ± 0.09 (maxbias) for 1/P_gm versus constrained feasible-region size
speedup_claims.conditions: asymptotic scaling in n with l fixed, and in l with n fixed; based on fitted scaling of inverse ground-state probability
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a fitted scaling from small-scale simulations, not a proven asymptotic speedup; the paper describes it as an indication of quantum advantage.

speedup_claims.factor: 1.32x (from 1/0.76) for warm-started and 1.96x (from 1/0.51) for maxbias, relative exponent ratio
speedup_claims.conditions: interpreted from fitted exponents in Fig. 11(a)
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an exponent-ratio comparison, not a direct runtime speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: 1.52x (from 1/0.66) for warm-started and 0.90x (from 1/1.11) for maxbias, relative exponent ratio
speedup_claims.conditions: interpreted from fitted exponents in Fig. 11(b)
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an exponent-ratio comparison, not a direct runtime speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Cost operator depth O(N); hard mixer depth O(L) with L=1 for nearest-neighbour mixer
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly given; classical feasible-region sampling scales exponentially in n and l

experiments.description: Warm-started QAOA portfolio solver on the DGMVP, using ranked warm-start initial state and the same hard mixer, evaluated across problem sizes and compared to classical baselines.

algorithm.variant: DGMVP QAOA with ranked warm-start initial state
algorithm.ansatz: Alternating cost operator and hard mixer M1(β)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Optimizer limited by I=2000 expectation-value evaluations per layer; final circuit evaluated after optimization
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Random initial ansatz parameters for the first layer; subsequent layers initialized with previous optimized parameters and new layer set to zero

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary block encoding with l bits per asset; warm-start state derived from rounded continuous GMVP solution
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_w w^T Σ w subject to budget, no-short, and discretization constraints
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard mixer preserves feasibility; warm-start initial state is feasible by construction; post-selection used in some noisy experiments
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Same DGMVP Hamiltonian C as in exp_1

problem_instance.description: Randomly generated DGMVP instances from market covariance matrices; scalability tested over n and l

dataset_specification.description: 32 stocks from NASDAQ and NYSE; daily adjusted-close prices from 2023-03-01 to 2023-06-30; covariance matrices built from 100 days of data

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Continuous GMVP solution computed classically, then rounded to binary precision a to form warm-start state
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 random DGMVP instances; metrics α_mean, α_min, P_min, and P_gm; statevector reconstruction used for scaling plots

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Warm-start from rounded continuous GMVP solution; binary precision a = 1/(2^l - 1)
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute approximation ratios and probabilities from sampled bitstrings; statevector used to remove sampling noise in scaling analysis

speedup_claims.factor: 1/P_gm scales as a·B(n,l)^b with b = 0.76 ± 0.30 (warm-started) and b = 0.51 ± 0.09 (maxbias) versus constrained feasible-region size
speedup_claims.conditions: scaling in n with l=3 and in l with n=4; unfrozen-layerwise optimization; DA with Nm=16 and I=2000
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper frames this as favorable scaling and a possible indication of quantum advantage, not a proven asymptotic speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: 1/P_gm scaling exponent ratio 1.32x (warm-started) and 1.96x (maxbias) relative to classical constrained sampling
1/P_gm scaling exponent ratio 1.52x (warm-started) and 0.90x (maxbias) relative to classical constrained sampling

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Hard mixer depth O(L) with L=1; cost operator depth O(N)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Constrained feasible-region sampling scales as B(n,l) = binomial(2l+n-2, n-1)

experiments.description: Comparison of hard mixer variants M1(β) and M2(β) on the DGMVP, including loss-landscape smoothness and optimization difficulty.

algorithm.ansatz: Alternating cost operator with hard mixers M1(β) and M2(β)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Fixed-ansatz optimization over p layers; no explicit convergence threshold reported
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Random initial parameters for fixed-ansatz runs; β and γ sampled uniformly for the random-state comparison

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary block encoding with l=5 in mixer-landscape study

problem_instance.description: Randomly generated DGMVP instances from market covariance matrices

dataset_specification.description: Covariance matrices from 32 stocks; example landscape study uses n=4, l=5

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Covariance matrix from daily adjusted-close prices
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 simulations; scan β5 over [0,2π] with resolution π/500; finite-difference gradients; compare average gradient, largest gradient, min, max-min, and valley count

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Fix all parameters except β5; use finite-difference gradients on sampled approximation ratios
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Aggregate gradient statistics over 100 random instances

speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment compares mixer variants only; no classical baseline or speedup claim is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: M1 has depth O(1) per asset-distance layer with L=1; M2 has larger support and harder optimization

experiments.description: Layerwise optimization study comparing frozen-layerwise, unfrozen-layerwise, and fixed-ansatz training for the DGMVP QAOA.

algorithm.ansatz: Alternating cost operator and hard mixer M1(β)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Layerwise growth until p=5; each added layer optimized with I' expectation-value evaluations
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Start with p'=1 and random initial parameters; new layers initialized to zero (identity layer)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary block encoding with n=l=4 in the layerwise benchmark
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard mixer preserves feasibility; layerwise identity layers preserve prior optimization

problem_instance.description: Fixed DGMVP instance from market covariance matrix

dataset_specification.description: n=4, l=4 benchmark instance; covariance from 32-stock market basket

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Covariance matrix from daily adjusted-close prices
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 100 random initial parameter seeds for p=1; compare mean α_mean and median α_min across p

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Initialize new layer parameters to zero; carry forward optimized parameters from previous layer
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute α_mean and α_min statistics over 100 runs; compare percentiles

speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment is an optimizer comparison (frozen-layerwise, unfrozen-layerwise, fixed ansatz) and does not report a classical baseline.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Layerwise circuit depth grows with p; hard mixer depth O(L)=O(1) for L=1

experiments.description: Noise-robustness experiment for the DGMVP QAOA under thermal-relaxation noise, with and without post-selection during optimization.

algorithm.ansatz: Alternating cost operator and hard mixer M1(β)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Fixed-ansatz optimization; no explicit convergence threshold reported

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary block encoding with n=l=4 in the noise study
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection enforces budget constraint Eq. (2a) during noisy optimization; unfiltered noisy optimization also tested

problem_instance.description: Fixed DGMVP instance from market covariance matrix

dataset_specification.description: n=4, l=4 benchmark instance; covariance from 32-stock market basket

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Covariance matrix from daily adjusted-close prices
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Over 100 simulations with random initial parameters; compare α_mean and post-selection probability P_ps as functions of Nm and p

noise_model.mitigation_details: Post-select states satisfying the budget constraint Eq. (2a); compare filtered vs unfiltered noisy optimization

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate thermal-relaxation noise ensemble from sampled T1/T2 values
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Estimate α_mean and P_ps from noisy samples; compare with noiseless reference

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports noise degradation and post-selection overhead, not a speedup over a classical baseline.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Noise and post-selection increase effective shot cost by roughly an order of magnitude to maintain fixed stochastic noise
